candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of the Watchers (1 Enoch 1-36)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of the Watchers (1 Enoch 1-36) (c. 200 BC)

'Before these things Enoch was hidden, and no one of the children of men knew where he was hidden, and where he abode, and what had become of him' — the foundational text for Enoch's hidden pre-translation existence. Already before the Flood narrative, Enoch is 'hidden' (Geez xəbu') with the watchers and holy ones — translated from ordinary human existence into the angelic order. This Tewahedo reads as the foundation of Enoch's authority to receive subsequent visions: he is the human-yet-translated witness, qualified to mediate between angelic and human knowledge precisely because he occupies both spheres.

candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of the Watchers (1 Enoch 1-36)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of the Watchers (1 Enoch 1-36) (c. 200 BC)

The angels commission Enoch: 'Enoch, thou scribe of righteousness, go, declare to the Watchers of the heaven who have left the high heaven, the holy eternal place, and have defiled themselves with women' — Enoch's prophetic-judicial role as scribe. Where ordinary scribes record human events, Enoch is the scribe of the angelic-judicial process: the divine sentence on the Watchers passes THROUGH Enoch's recording. The title 'scribe of righteousness' (ṣaḥafe ṣədq) becomes the canonical Tewahedo designation; this verse is the textual warrant for treating Enoch's recorded visions as inspired prophetic Scripture rather than mere human composition.
